#!/usr/bin/env bash
# DeepSeek Harness Web launcher (WSL edition)
# Generated by dsh-wsl-launcher v__VERSION__ -- this file is rewritten on
# every install; do not edit by hand.
#
# Behavior (default "web" action):
#   1. Make sure `node` is on PATH: wsl.exe --exec starts a non-interactive,
#      non-login bash, so ~/.bashrc and ~/.profile (where nvm is sourced)
#      never run, and the dsh bin shim would die with `exec: node: not found`.
#   2. Find the dsh CLI: PATH first, then the interactive login shell
#      (covers nvm), then the install path recorded by the plugin.
#   3. If the Web UI port already listens, just open the Windows browser.
#   4. Otherwise start `dsh web --port <PORT>` DETACHED: its own session
#      (setsid), no controlling terminal, output appended to the log file
#      below. The console window then closes like a normal program while
#      the server keeps running inside the WSL distribution.
#   5. Poll the port until it is ready, then open the Windows browser.
#
# Usage: <script> [web|stop] [--port N]
# Actions:
#   web   (default) start-if-needed + open the browser
#   stop  stop the background server started by this launcher
#
# Environment:
#   DSH_WEB_LAUNCHER_FOREGROUND=1  legacy mode: run `dsh web` in this
#      console and keep the window open while it runs (debugging).
#   DSH_BIN    explicit path to the dsh executable (skips auto-detection;
#      use it when dsh lives somewhere unusual).
#   NODE_BIN   explicit path to the node executable (skips auto-detection).
#
# The background daemon is started with DSH_WEB_AUTOSTOP=1, so the server
# shuts itself down when every browser tab of the Web UI is closed (when
# no tab has reconnected for ~30s). Double-click the shortcut again to
# start it back up.

set -u

PORT=__PORT__
URL=__URL__
DSH_BIN_FALLBACK='__DSH_BIN__'
LAUNCH_MODE='__LAUNCH_MODE__'
NPX_PACKAGE='__NPX_PACKAGE__'
READY_TRIES=120

# Parse argv: [web|stop] [--port N]. The desktop shortcut always passes
# `--port <port>` (harmless echo of the baked-in value); a bare positional
# argument selects the action. Unknown flags are ignored (forward compat).
ACTION="web"
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        web | stop)
            if [ "$ACTION" = "web" ]; then ACTION="$1"; fi
            shift ;;
        --port=*)
            PORT="${1#--port=}"; shift ;;
        --port)
            if [ "$#" -ge 2 ]; then PORT="$2"; shift; fi
            shift ;;
        *)
            shift ;;
    esac
done
URL="http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}"

LAUNCHER_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
LOG_FILE="${LAUNCHER_DIR}/web-${PORT}.log"
PID_FILE="${LAUNCHER_DIR}/web-${PORT}.pid"
LOCK_DIR="${LAUNCHER_DIR}/web-${PORT}.lock"

log()  { printf '[dsh-wsl-launcher] %s\n' "$*"; }
# fail() also tees to the log file: when the script runs from a hidden
# console (desktop shortcut), the console output is invisible, and the log
# is the only place an error message can be found.
fail() {
    printf '[dsh-wsl-launcher][error] %s\n' "$*" >&2
    printf '%s [launcher][error] %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*" >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
}

hold() {
    # Keep the console open so an error message is actually readable.
    # Bounded on purpose: a hidden console (desktop shortcut) still has a
    # tty, but nobody can press Enter -- without the timeout the script
    # would sit blocked on read forever and leave a zombie session behind.
    if [ -t 0 ]; then
        read -r -t 30 -p "Press Enter to close this window (auto-closes in 30s)..." _ || true
    fi
}

# Locate the dsh executable, in order:
#   1. $DSH_BIN -- explicit override (export it if your dsh lives in an
#      unusual place, e.g. /opt/dsh/bin/dsh)
#   2. bare PATH -- works when launched from a full shell
#   3. an interactive shell -- loads ~/.bashrc / ~/.profile (nvm, npm
#      global prefixes, volta, ... normally land on PATH there)
#   4. well-known home of common Node package managers
#   5. the baked-in fallback (the dsh that installed this launcher)
resolve_dsh() {
    local found cand
    if [ -n "${DSH_BIN:-}" ] && [ -x "$DSH_BIN" ]; then
        printf '%s' "$DSH_BIN"; return 0
    fi
    found="$(command -v dsh 2>/dev/null)" || true
    if [ -n "${found:-}" ]; then printf '%s' "$found"; return 0; fi
    found="$(bash -ic 'command -v dsh' 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)" || true
    if [ -n "${found:-}" ] && [ -x "${found:-}" ]; then printf '%s' "$found"; return 0; fi
    for cand in \
        "$HOME"/.local/bin/dsh \
        "$HOME"/.npm-global/bin/dsh \
        "$HOME"/.local/share/pnpm/dsh \
        "$HOME"/.volta/bin/dsh \
        "$HOME"/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/*/installation/bin/dsh \
        "$HOME"/.local/share/mise/installs/node/*/bin/dsh \
        "$HOME"/.local/share/mise/shims/dsh \
        /usr/local/bin/dsh \
        /usr/bin/dsh; do
        if [ -x "$cand" ]; then printf '%s' "$cand"; return 0; fi
    done
    if [ -n "${DSH_BIN_FALLBACK:-}" ] && [ -x "$DSH_BIN_FALLBACK" ]; then
        printf '%s' "$DSH_BIN_FALLBACK"; return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# Resolve npx only in the explicit npx mode. It must come from the same
# Node installation as node whenever possible.
resolve_npx() {
    local n
    if [ -n "${NPX_BIN:-}" ] && [ -x "$NPX_BIN" ]; then
        printf '%s' "$NPX_BIN"; return 0
    fi
    n="$(command -v npx 2>/dev/null)" || true
    if [ -n "${n:-}" ] && [ -x "$n" ]; then printf '%s' "$n"; return 0; fi
    if [ -n "${NODE_DIR:-}" ] && [ -x "${NODE_DIR}/npx" ]; then
        printf '%s' "${NODE_DIR}/npx"; return 0
    fi
    n="$(bash -lic 'command -v npx' 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)" || true
    if [ -n "${n:-}" ] && [ -x "$n" ]; then printf '%s' "$n"; return 0; fi
    return 1
}

# Locate a node executable even when PATH is bare (GUI shortcut launch),
# in order:
#   1. $NODE_BIN -- explicit override
#   2. PATH, then the user's login+interactive shell (loads ~/.profile,
#      where nvm & friends normally put node on PATH)
#   3. well-known version-manager layouts: nvm / fnm / mise (newest
#      installed version first), then volta, then system paths.
resolve_node() {
    local n cand
    if [ -n "${NODE_BIN:-}" ] && [ -x "$NODE_BIN" ]; then
        printf '%s' "$NODE_BIN"; return 0
    fi
    n="$(command -v node 2>/dev/null)" || true
    if [ -n "${n:-}" ]; then printf '%s' "$n"; return 0; fi
    n="$(bash -lic 'command -v node' 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)" || true
    if [ -n "${n:-}" ] && [ -x "$n" ]; then printf '%s' "$n"; return 0; fi
    cand="$(ls -1d "$HOME"/.nvm/versions/node/*/bin \
                    "$HOME"/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/*/installation/bin \
                    "$HOME"/.local/share/mise/installs/node/*/bin 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -n 1)" || true
    if [ -n "${cand:-}" ] && [ -x "${cand:-}/node" ]; then printf '%s' "${cand}/node"; return 0; fi
    for cand in "$HOME"/.volta/bin/node "$HOME"/.local/bin/node /usr/local/bin/node /usr/bin/node; do
        if [ -x "$cand" ]; then printf '%s' "$cand"; return 0; fi
    done
    return 1
}

# Probe the loopback port with bash /dev/tcp -- no curl/netcat required.
port_open() {
    (exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${PORT}") 2>/dev/null
}

# Open the Windows default browser. Tries, in order:
#   1. explorer.exe <url>                  (the usual WSL interop path)
#   2. powershell.exe Start-Process <url>  (works where explorer.exe does not,
#                                          e.g. containerized WSL)
#   3. cmd.exe /c start "" <url>           (classic fallback)
# and finally prints the URL when nothing works.
open_browser() {
    local exe="" ps="" cmd=""
    exe="$(command -v explorer.exe 2>/dev/null)" || true
    if [ -z "${exe:-}" ] && [ -x /mnt/c/Windows/explorer.exe ]; then
        exe="/mnt/c/Windows/explorer.exe"
    fi
    if [ -n "$exe" ]; then
        "$exe" "$URL" >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "Windows browser launch command returned an error; check WSL interop."
        log "requested one browser tab for ${URL}"
        return 0
    fi
    ps="$(command -v powershell.exe 2>/dev/null)" || true
    if [ -z "${ps:-}" ] && [ -x /mnt/c/Windows/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe ]; then
        ps="/mnt/c/Windows/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe"
    fi
    if [ -n "$ps" ]; then
        DSH_URL="$URL" "$ps" -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "Start-Process \$env:DSH_URL" >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
            log "Windows browser launch command returned an error; check WSL interop."
        log "requested one browser tab for ${URL}"
        return 0
    fi
    cmd="$(command -v cmd.exe 2>/dev/null)" || true
    if [ -z "${cmd:-}" ] && [ -x /mnt/c/Windows/System32/cmd.exe ]; then
        cmd="/mnt/c/Windows/System32/cmd.exe"
    fi
    if [ -n "$cmd" ]; then
        "$cmd" /c start "" "$URL" >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "Windows browser launch command returned an error; check WSL interop."
        log "requested one browser tab for ${URL}"
        return 0
    fi
    log "could not launch the Windows browser (WSL interop disabled?)."
    log "open this URL manually: ${URL}"
    return 0
}

pid_alive() {
    [ -n "${1:-}" ] && kill -0 "$1" 2>/dev/null
}

read_pid() {
    [ -f "$PID_FILE" ] || return 1
    local pid
    pid="$(cat "$PID_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
    pid="${pid//$'\r'/}"
    pid="${pid//$'\n'/}"
    case "$pid" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
    [ "$pid" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null || return 1
    printf '%s' "$pid"
}

controlled_pid() {
    local pid="$1" cmdline identity
    cmdline="$(tr '\0' ' ' < "/proc/${pid}/cmdline" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    case "$cmdline" in *dsh*web*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
    identity="$(ps -o pid= -o pgid= -o sid= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1, $2, $3}')"
    [ "$identity" = "$pid $pid $pid" ]
}

acquire_lock() {
    if mkdir "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
        printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$LOCK_DIR/pid"
        trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
        return 0
    fi
    local owner
    owner="$(cat "$LOCK_DIR/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -n "$owner" ] && kill -0 "$owner" 2>/dev/null; then
        fail "another launcher operation is already running for port ${PORT}"
        return 1
    fi
    rm -rf "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
    if mkdir "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
        printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$LOCK_DIR/pid"
        trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
        return 0
    fi
    fail "could not acquire launcher lock: ${LOCK_DIR}"
    return 1
}

tail_log() {
    if [ -f "$LOG_FILE" ] && [ -s "$LOG_FILE" ]; then
        log "last log lines (${LOG_FILE}):"
        tail -n 15 "$LOG_FILE" | sed 's/^/    /'
    fi
}

stop_background() {
    local pid
    pid="$(read_pid)" || pid=""
    if pid_alive "$pid" && controlled_pid "$pid"; then
        log "stopping dsh web (pid ${pid})..."
        # The daemon is the leader of its own process group (setsid); kill
        # the group so child processes go down with it. The plain-kill
        # fallback covers daemons started without setsid.
        kill -TERM -- -"$pid" 2>/dev/null || {
            fail "dsh web process group ${pid} is no longer controlled"
            return 1
        }
        local i=0
        while [ "$i" -lt 40 ] && pid_alive "$pid"; do
            sleep 0.5
            i=$((i + 1))
        done
        if pid_alive "$pid"; then
            kill -KILL -- -"$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        rm -f "$PID_FILE"
        if port_open; then
            fail "pid ${pid} is gone but port ${PORT} still listens; another process may own it now."
            return 1
        fi
        log "dsh web stopped."
        return 0
    fi
    rm -f "$PID_FILE"
    if port_open; then
        fail "no launcher pid file (or its process is gone) but port ${PORT} still listens."
        fail "the server was probably started outside this launcher; stop it where it was started."
        hold
        return 1
    fi
    log "dsh web is not running (nothing to stop)."
    return 0
}

# First line of every run, so the log proves the script started at all
# (the hidden-console shortcut leaves no other trace when it fails early).
printf '%s [launcher] invoked (action=%s, pid=%s, tty=%s)\n' \
    "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$ACTION" "$$" "$([ -t 0 ] && echo yes || echo no)" \
    >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true

case "$ACTION" in
    stop)
        acquire_lock || exit 1
        stop_background
        exit $?
        ;;
    web) ;;
    *)
        fail "unknown action: ${ACTION} (expected: web, stop)"
        hold
        exit 2
        ;;
esac

# GUI-launched shells (wsl.exe --exec /bin/bash script.sh) are
# non-interactive and non-login: ~/.bashrc (dsh on PATH) and ~/.profile
# (nvm node) are both skipped, and the dsh bin shim is a /bin/sh script
# that ends in `exec node ...`. Without a node on PATH it dies with
# `exec: node: not found` -- so restore one here, before anything runs.
NODE_BIN="$(resolve_node)" || {
    fail "node was not found in this WSL distribution."
    fail "wsl.exe --exec does not load ~/.profile, so a version-manager node (nvm, fnm, asdf) is missing from PATH."
    hold
    exit 1
}
NODE_DIR="$(dirname "$NODE_BIN")"
case ":${PATH:-}:" in
    *":${NODE_DIR}:"*) ;;
    *)
        PATH="${NODE_DIR}:${PATH:-}"
        export PATH
        log "extended PATH with ${NODE_DIR} (node ${NODE_BIN})"
        ;;
esac

if [ "$LAUNCH_MODE" = "npx" ]; then
    NPX_BIN="$(resolve_npx)" || {
        fail "npx was not found in this WSL distribution."
        fail "install Node.js with npm/npx, then retry the launcher."
        hold
        exit 1
    }
    log "using explicit npx package: ${NPX_PACKAGE}"
else
    DSH_BIN="$(resolve_dsh)" || {
        fail "dsh was not found in this WSL distribution."
        fail "install it first, e.g.: npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh"
        fail "or configure launchMode: npx with an exact npxPackage."
        hold
        exit 1
    }
    log "using dsh: ${DSH_BIN}"
fi

if port_open; then
    log "server already listening on 127.0.0.1:${PORT} -- opening browser"
    open_browser
    exit 0
fi

if [ "${DSH_WEB_LAUNCHER_FOREGROUND:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    log "foreground mode: ${LAUNCH_MODE} web --port ${PORT}"
    log "keep this window open -- closing it stops the server"
    if [ "$LAUNCH_MODE" = "npx" ]; then
        exec "${NPX_BIN}" --yes "${NPX_PACKAGE}" web --port "${PORT}"
    fi
    exec "${DSH_BIN}" web --port "${PORT}"
fi

acquire_lock || exit 1
log "starting dsh web in the background (this window will close; the server keeps running)..."
log "log file: ${LOG_FILE}"
: >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || {
    fail "cannot write the log file: ${LOG_FILE}"
    hold
    exit 1
}
# Start the detached daemon and record its pid.
#   setsid: own session, no controlling terminal -- the server survives this
#   script (and the console window) exiting. nohup: ignore SIGHUP. All
#   output is appended to the log file. Without setsid, degrade to plain
#   nohup. --no-open: the web server opens a browser tab itself by
#   default; the launcher opens exactly one tab (below), so suppress the
#   server's own to avoid two tabs per double-click.
start_daemon() {
    # DSH_WEB_AUTOSTOP=1: the dsh-web-autostop feature of this plugin --
    # the server shuts itself down when every browser tab is closed.
    # DSH_WEB_LAUNCHER_LOG: the server writes a note there before stopping,
    # so the shutdown is visible in this launcher's log.
    if [ "$LAUNCH_MODE" = "npx" ]; then
        if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            setsid nohup env DSH_WEB_AUTOSTOP=1 DSH_WEB_LAUNCHER_LOG="$LOG_FILE" \
                "${NPX_BIN}" --yes "${NPX_PACKAGE}" web --port "${PORT}" --no-open >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 </dev/null &
        else
            nohup env DSH_WEB_AUTOSTOP=1 DSH_WEB_LAUNCHER_LOG="$LOG_FILE" \
                "${NPX_BIN}" --yes "${NPX_PACKAGE}" web --port "${PORT}" --no-open >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 </dev/null &
        fi
    elif command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        setsid nohup env DSH_WEB_AUTOSTOP=1 DSH_WEB_LAUNCHER_LOG="$LOG_FILE" \
            "${DSH_BIN}" web --port "${PORT}" --no-open >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 </dev/null &
    else
        nohup env DSH_WEB_AUTOSTOP=1 DSH_WEB_LAUNCHER_LOG="$LOG_FILE" \
            "${DSH_BIN}" web --port "${PORT}" --no-open >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 </dev/null &
    fi
    DSH_PID=$!
    echo "$DSH_PID" > "$PID_FILE"
}

# Double-click race: two invocations may both see a closed port before
# either daemon binds it (the server takes a few seconds to come up). If a
# live pidfile appeared, a sibling invocation won the race -- join its wait
# instead of starting a second daemon, which would crash on EADDRINUSE and
# clobber the pidfile with a dead pid, breaking later `stop`.
if [ -f "$PID_FILE" ] && DSH_PID="$(read_pid)" && kill -0 "$DSH_PID" 2>/dev/null && controlled_pid "$DSH_PID"; then
    log "another launcher instance already started the daemon (pid ${DSH_PID}) -- joining its startup wait"
else
    start_daemon
fi

tries=0
while ! port_open; do
    tries=$((tries + 1))
    if [ "$tries" -gt "$READY_TRIES" ]; then
        fail "server did not open port ${PORT} in time (about 60s)."
        tail_log
        hold
        exit 1
    fi
    if ! kill -0 "$DSH_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
        fail "dsh web exited early -- see ${LOG_FILE}"
        tail_log
        hold
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 0.5
done

log "server ready -- opening browser"
log "it now runs in the background; to stop it later: 'bash ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} stop' (or ask your agent: wsl_launcher stop)"
open_browser
exit 0
